newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: CRICKET-QUEENSLAND CRUSH W.AUSTRALIA IN SHIELD FINAL.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-QUEENSLAND CRUSH W.AUSTRALIA IN SHIELD FINAL.

text.p: Queensland thrashed Western Australia by 160 runs to win the domestic Sheffield Shield title on Tuesday and provide fast bowler Adam Dale with double cause for celebration.
Dale, selected by Australia on Tuesday for the upcoming limited overs series against South Africa to replace injured fast bowler Glenn McGrath, claimed match figures of nine for 84.
After waiting 69 years to taste success in the domestic first-class competition, Queensland's away win in Perth gave them their second Shield title in the past three seasons.
But their victory party was delayed by Western Australia captain and all-rounder Tom Moody, who hit 152 in a marathon innings lasting almost seven hours at the WACA Ground.
Moody, who arrived at the crease with his side reeling on 18 for four on Monday, faced 334 balls and hit 15 fours and one six.
Needing only a draw in the final to lift the Shield on the strength of their superior record in reaching the five-day final, Western Australia were comprehensively outplayed.
Resuming on 166 for five, Western Australia survived until the afternoon session before being dismissed for 304 in their second innings.
Wicketkeeper Adam Gilchrist, also named by selectors on Tuesday for the seven-match one-day series in South Africa as a replacement for Ian Healy, supported Moody with a gritty 48.
The match was a triumph for veteran Queensland opener Trevor Barsby, who scored a century and a half-century in his last appearance before retirement.
Queensland, who dismissed Western Australia for 165 in the first innings, scored 320 and 309 to set up the victory.
